sentences.text: Tamarro is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur named after a local mythological creature.
Analysis indicates the holotype was a subadult that experienced rapid early growth.

The only known species, Tamarro insperatus, is represented by a partial metatarsal fossil described in 2021. The holotype specimen, a metatarsal found in 2003 at the Sant Romà d'Abella site, belongs to the Talarn Formation. Sellés and colleagues formally described the genus and species Tamarro insperatus in 2021. The specific name insperatus means "unexpected" because the fossil was an unexpected find.
Tamarro is classified in the subfamily Jinfengopteryginae, representing the first European member of this group.
Researchers suggest that Tamarro's ancestors migrated from Asia to Europe between the Cenomanian and Maastrichtian stages.
Tamarro lived on the Ibero-Armorican Island during the Late Cretaceous. Tamarro lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Tamarro coexisted with dwarf sauropods and lambeosaurine hadrosaurs.
